question.text: Consider the figure provided. \(1 \mathrm{~mol}\) of an ideal gas is kept in a cylinder, fitted with a piston, at the position A, at \(18^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\). If the piston is moved to position \(\mathrm{B}\), keeping the temperature unchanged, then ' \(x\) ' \(L\) atm work is done in this reversible process. \(x=\) ______ \(\mathrm{L}\) atm. (nearest integer) [Given : Absolute temperature \(={ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}+273.15, \mathrm{R}=0.08206 \mathrm{~L} \mathrm{~atm} \mathrm{~mol}{ }^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}\) ]

solution.text:
$\begin{aligned} & \omega=-n R T \ln \left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right) \\ & =-1 \times \cdot 08206 \times 291 \cdot 15 \ln \left(\frac{100}{10}\right) \\ & =-55.0128\end{aligned}$
Work done by system $\approx 55 \mathrm{~atm}$ lit.
